Looks like this project only lives on your machine right now—there’s no remote configured for `.git`, so there isn’t a repo URL to hand your contractor. To give them access you have two options:

- Host it somewhere (e.g. GitHub): create a new empty repo in your account, then from `opalclone/` run ```git remote add origin <the repo URL>``` followed by ```git push -u origin main``` (or whatever branch you want them on). Share that URL.
- Zip and send: from the parent directory run ```zip -r opalclone.zip opalclone``` and send the resulting archive through whatever channel you use.

If they truly just need a screenshot of the repo tab, open the repo in Finder/GitHub Desktop/Xcode and take a screenshot (macOS shortcut `⌘⇧4` lets you capture a selection).
what does he mean by tab screenshot

He probably wants visual proof that the repo exists—i.e. a screenshot of the browser tab showing the repository page (the “Code” tab on GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket). If you’re not hosting it yet, that’s why he’s asking for the repo link instead. You could either:

- Push the project to a hosting service and send him the URL.  
- Or take a screenshot of the repo page once it’s hosted (open the repo in your browser, make sure the “Code” tab is active, then use `⌘⇧4` on macOS to grab that portion).

If you’re unsure, just ask him which tab he needs—some developers call the main repo overview the “repo tab.”
